text:
### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, exactly one of five alternative activities ran in each case between A43 and A28: A14 in about 17 in 100 cases, A17 in about 25, A18 in about 27, A19 in about 14, and A20 in about 19 (the shares sum to all cases, and no two of them ever occurred in the same case). Each of the five was always followed by A28, and A43 preceded it. [OCC001, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, DIR001, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR011, REL003, REL029, REL035, REL036]

- In the later window, none of A14, A17, A18, A19, A20 was observed in any of the 200 cases, while five other activities — A15, A16, A25, A26, A27 — each ran in all 200 cases, exactly once per case and never repeated. In the earlier window these five had not been observed at all. [OCC001, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC002, OCC003, OCC008, OCC009, OCC010]

- The new five run together in the same cases without a fixed order: every pair co-occurs in all cases and either order occurs roughly half the time (for example, A15 before A16 in about 52 in 100 cases and A16 before A15 in about 48; the other pairs fall between about 45 and 60 in 100). [REL010, REL015, REL016, REL017, REL024, REL025, REL026, REL051, REL052, REL055]

- A43's outgoing transitions switched completely: earlier they went only to A14, A17, A18, A19 and A20 (roughly 14–27 in 100 each); later only to A15, A16, A25, A26 and A27 (roughly 17–25 in 100 each). Each new activity follows A43 and precedes A28 in all 200 cases, and each is followed either by one of the other four or by A28. [DIR011, DIR002, DIR003, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010, REL018, REL019, REL027, REL028, REL053, REL054, REL056, REL057, REL058, REL059]

- Consistent with five activities now sitting between A43 and A28 instead of one, A28's mean event position moved later (about 0.39 to 0.47 of the trace) and A43's moved earlier (about 0.32 to 0.29); these are event positions, not clock times. [POS011, POS012]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the segment between A43 and A28 was restructured from a one-of-five choice into a mandatory five-activity block: in the earlier window each case executed exactly one of A14, A17, A18, A19 or A20 between A43 and A28, whereas in the later window every case executes A15, A16, A25, A26 and A27, each once and in varying order, still between A43 and A28. The signs are direct and consistent: all-or-nothing participation on both sides, a complete switch of A43's outgoing transitions from the old five to the new five, every new activity co-occurring with and being ordered between A43 and A28 in 200 of 200 cases, and opposite position shifts of A43 and A28. Every item's difference also exceeds about 995 in 1000 random re-splits of the pooled data, and with 92 qualifying control-flow items against roughly 0.72 expected if nothing had changed, chance sampling cannot explain the pattern as a whole. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, OCC010, DIR011, REL018, REL019, POS011, POS012]

Limitations: the indicators are computed from the same traces, so the agreeing items are not independent confirmations; the evidence cannot establish whether the new activities are relabelled or re-implemented versions of the old ones, and it cannot rule out that the two windows sample different process variants or subpopulations rather than reflecting a modification at the change point. Zero participation means an activity was not observed in that window's sample, not proof of removal.
